newsitem.title: CANADA: Heavy rain, snow slow Alberta harvest progress.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain, snow slow Alberta harvest progress.

text.p: Alberta made little harvest progress in the week to Monday due to heavy amounts of snow and rain, Alberta Agriculture said in a crop update.

"The amount harvested has only marginally increased above fifty percent. Any crop being harvested at this time is coming off with a high moisture content and therefore must be dried before going in the bin," it said.
Moisture levels were said to be around 18 to 22 percent.
The most significant combining progress was made in the eastern half of the province and the northern tip of the Peace River Region (Fort Vermilion and Manning), the report said.

"At this time yields are holding fairly close to the estimates given in the Crop Report in September. These yields will be negatively impacted slightly, however, as more and more producers are noticing sprouting in their crops and as incidences of crop mold become more prevalent," it added.

The outlook for this week was expected to be more promising. Dry winds and sunshine over the weekend and in the early part of this week could have producers going full speed by the ninth or tenth of October, the report said.
"Given ten to 14 days of good weather, Alberta farmers could finally get the 1996 crop in the bin," it said.
